thesis: The coherent short thesis is that Planet is valued as an emerging data/AI platform while its economics may remain those of a capital-intensive satellite and government-contracting business. Q2 growth and backlog are real, but owner FCF is obscured by working-capital inflows, SBC, fleet capex and equity issuance. If large sovereign contracts normalize, raw imagery commoditizes, or dilution persists, the stock can fall toward the locked Base/Bear values even without business failure. Current evidence does not prove accounting impairment, financing dependence, moat collapse, subsidy-driven demand or fatal single-customer dependence.

evidence.claim: FY27 H1 reported FCF was $21.3M, but operating cash flow benefited from a $47.1M deferred-revenue increase and $23.9M receivables decline, making cash conversion look stronger than normalized owner economics may be.
H1 SBC was $33.5M and the company raised $122.4M gross through ATM issuance plus $107.8M from warrant exercises, creating meaningful per-share dilution risk.
FY27 capex guidance is $100M-$115M against revenue guidance of $430M-$441M, so the business remains materially capital intensive at its current scale.
evidence.value: Capex roughly one-quarter of guided revenue

evidence.claim: Three Q2 customers represented 17%, 11% and 10% of revenue, so contract timing and concentration can materially affect reported growth.
The locked DCF is about $5.22 Bear, $15.94 Base and $39.36 Bull versus $16.99, showing that execution disappointment can produce large downside without insolvency.
Against the short thesis, FY26 NDR was 116%, recurring ACV is 98%, RPO/backlog are large and liquid assets were about $865M, confirming real customer demand and substantial survival runway.

counterevidence: The longitudinal archive and daily cadence can create a data advantage that raw-imagery competitors cannot reproduce quickly.
98% recurring ACV, NDR above 100% and contracted backlog argue that demand is not primarily promotional or speculative.
Net liquidity and positive H1 FCF make near-term forced financing unlikely even under weaker equity markets.
ATM shares were issued at prices materially above the frozen price, so recent issuance was not necessarily economically destructive if reinvestment returns are adequate.
unknowns: Normalized owner FCF margin after full fleet replacement capex and working-capital normalization.
Long-run net dilution from SBC, ATM capacity, warrants and convertible settlement.
Gross-margin profile of sovereign satellite services versus data subscriptions.
Pricing power and switching cost as rival constellations expand.
Whether agentic AI becomes a paid high-margin layer or remains a feature supporting imagery demand.
falsifiers: Owner FCF/share compounds strongly while capex intensity and net dilution both decline.
Customer concentration falls and RPO converts broadly with stable or improving gross margin.
AI/data products materially raise ARPU, retention and margins without requiring proportional satellite capex.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손
hard_veto_flags.rationale: FY2026 ICFR was effective and independently attested; the principal issue is economic interpretation of non-GAAP/cash-flow metrics, not evidence of accounting unreliability.
Planet has substantial liquid assets and positive H1 FCF; recent equity issuance is material but not currently required for near-term survival.
High recurring ACV, NDR above 100%, renewals and contracted demand show real willingness to pay.
Full-cycle incremental ROIC remains unproven, but current revenue growth, backlog and emerging FCF do not demonstrate structural collapse.
Competition and multi-sourcing are real, but current retention, archive accumulation and expanded sensor capabilities do not show persistent moat contraction.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 단일 제품·단일 고객·단일 규제에 대한 치명적 종속성
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Customer concentration is high but no single customer is fatal, and revenue spans multiple products, use cases, geographies and government/commercial buyers.

Recent ATM, warrant and SBC dilution is economically material. The domain owners RF and FS must determine whether it clears; persistent mid-to-high single-digit net dilution after sustainable FCF would support confirmation.

key_kpis.name: Normalized owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: Growth after working-capital normalization must exceed diluted-share growth

key_kpis.name: Net dilution
key_kpis.threshold: Move toward low-single-digit annual share growth or less after FCF breakeven

key_kpis.name: Customer concentration / RPO conversion
key_kpis.threshold: Concentration declines while contracted demand converts with stable margins

next_checks: FY27 Q3 owner-FCF bridge and share-count change.
Use of remaining ATM authorization and convertible settlement policy.
Customer concentration, sovereign-contract margins and AI monetization.
